analysis.one_liner: Infosys is one of India's largest IT services companies, providing software development, consulting and outsourcing to large global corporations, mainly billed in US dollars and euros.
analysis.whats_happening: Infosys reported Q2 FY27 results on Oct 23, 2026: revenue of $5.14bn grew just 1.5% YoY in constant currency, net profit rose 6.2% YoY to Rs 7,823 crore, and operating margin held at 21%. Management cut full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1-2% constant currency (from 1.5-3% earlier), citing pricing pressure and cautious client spending - the stock fell roughly 6-7% on the day. Separately, the company's Rs 26 interim dividend has its record date today, Nov 3, 2026, with payment on Nov 11; the next quarterly result (Q3 FY27) is tentatively expected mid-January 2027.
analysis.plain_terms: Infosys writes and maintains software for large companies abroad, and gets paid mostly in dollars and euros. The business itself is barely growing right now - just 1-2% a year in the currency it actually earns - even though the profit and margin numbers look stable. The tension: it's a very well-run, debt-free, cash-generative company, but demand for new IT projects from Western clients has been weak for a while, and AI tools are making some services cheaper to deliver, which pressures prices even when deal volumes hold up.
analysis.quarters: Reported INR revenue grew 10.7% YoY to Rs 49,244 crore, but this overstates the real business - in the currency Infosys actually earns (constant currency USD terms), revenue grew only 1.5% YoY and 1.2% QoQ; the gap is mostly rupee depreciation, not more work being done, so the two figures are not directly comparable. Net profit grew a more modest 6.2% YoY to Rs 7,823 crore, and operating margin was flat at 21%, within the company's long-stated 20-22% guided band. Management explicitly lowered FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1-2% CC (from 1.5-3%), pointing to pricing pressure (partly AI-led deflation in service pricing) and cautious client budgets, while flagging large deal wins of $5.2bn TCV (62% net new) and AI-linked revenue at 10.5% of the book, up 29% QoQ.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 38.8% from its Dec 2024 peak of Rs 1,858.51, and down 20% over one year versus the Nifty's -8.1% - a clear underperformer even against a weak market. Over 3 and 5 years it is down 10% and 22% respectively, while the Nifty gained 22% and 33% over the same periods. There is no demerger or spin-off in the recorded corporate-action history (only ordinary stock splits, which are already reflected in a split-adjusted price series), so this is a genuine, not an artifact-driven, multi-year loss of shareholder value. The peer (TCS) has also fallen over 3 and 5 years, suggesting this is largely a sector-wide IT services derating rather than an Infosys-specific failure.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 15.6x, Infosys trades at a sizeable discount (reportedly near 40%) to the IT sector/peer median of around 26x, despite return ratios (ROE ~31.7%, ROCE ~42.8%) that are well above sector norms. Why it's cheap: the market is pricing in the 1-2% constant-currency growth guidance and ongoing pricing pressure from AI-led service deflation, not a lack of quality. Whether that discount is justified depends on whether growth stays stuck near 1-2% (cheap for a reason) or re-accelerates (cheap mispricing) - this report does not take a view on which.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is weak and essentially volume-led right now - constant-currency revenue growth of just 1.5% YoY/1.2% QoQ is the real story, with margin holding steady at 21% rather than expanding to flatter the profit line. So this isn't a case of margin masking stagnant volumes; both volume growth and margin are roughly flat. The one bright spot is AI-linked revenue (10.5% of the book, +29% QoQ), but it remains too small to move the overall growth number yet.
analysis.health_read: Cash conversion is strong - free cash flow of $928 million in the quarter equalled 113% of net profit - and the balance sheet is debt-free with about $4.7 billion in cash. Financial risk is minimal here; the real risk sitting on this business is demand/pricing risk - cautious client budgets and AI-driven pricing deflation in services, not balance-sheet stress.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (the founding group) hold only 13.90% of the company (up slightly from 13.82%), with zero pledging reported. Foreign institutional investors hold about 27.4%, and domestic institutions (mutual funds, insurers) hold roughly 39-43% depending on the tracker used - trackers differ on the exact DII figure, flagged rather than averaged. Ownership is dominated by broad institutional/index money; there is no marquee individual investor (in the Rakesh Jhunjhunwala/Radhakishan Damani mould) on the public register.
strengths: ROE of ~31.7% and ROCE of ~42.8% with a debt-free balance sheet and about $4.7bn in cash
Free cash flow of $928m in Q2 FY27 equalled 113% of net profit - strong cash conversion
Large deal wins of $5.2bn TCV in the quarter, 62% net new business
Trades at roughly 15.6x P/E, about a 40% discount to peer median, despite superior return ratios
AI-linked revenue growing 29% QoQ, now 10.5% of total revenue
watchpoints: FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance was cut to 1-2% from 1.5-3%, signalling continued demand softness
Reported INR revenue growth of 10.7% is largely currency-driven; real constant-currency growth was only 1.5% YoY - not like-for-like
Stock is down 38.8% from its Dec 2024 peak and has underperformed the Nifty over 1, 3 and 5 years
A US investor notice/early-stage investigation has surfaced relating to disclosures around the Oct 23, 2026 results - at an early stage, no findings yet
Reports of trainee terminations and a BPM facility layoff (triggering a US WARN Act inquiry) sit alongside management's statement of no mass layoffs - worth watching for signs of deeper cost-cutting
analysis.one_thing: Whether constant-currency revenue growth climbs back above the newly guided 1-2% band in the next couple of quarters - that would signal the slowdown is bottoming rather than deepening.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 results cross-checked across FreePressJournal, a Yahoo Finance earnings-call summary and Infosys SEC 6-K filings - consistent on revenue, profit and margin. Valuation ratios (P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE) were cross-checked across multiple trackers; P/E ranged 14.7x-15.6x and P/B 4.76x-5.10x across sources, so the higher-confidence recent figures (~15.6x P/E, ROE ~31.7%, ROCE ~42.8%) were used. DII shareholding percentage varies between trackers (38.98% vs 42.85% for Sep 2026) and was flagged rather than resolved to one number. Promoter pledge confirmed at 0% from the shareholding trackers. The exact wording of management's guidance commentary was taken from secondary summaries of the earnings call, not the primary transcript.
